propositions: Attestation staleness messages name a fixed fictional list (description/AC/file_impact/children) instead of the actual components that changed, preventing operators from identifying the root cause of invalidation.

Ticking AC checkboxes does NOT invalidate attestations because checkbox state is normalized out of the material basis by _normalize_checkbox_state before hashing, but the current message does not say this.

Pre-330c attestations that hashed raw descriptions cannot be matched by normalized recomputes or legacy grandfather logic when description boxes are ticked, producing spurious stale-material verdicts with no actual component edit.

The material basis is a single composite sha256 over exactly four keys (ticket_id, description, file_impact, children) plus file_impact_scope when scope is none, but per-component hashes are not recorded in the signed manifest, making it impossible to name which component changed.

Attestation refusal surfaces across generation.py, resign.py, completion.py, and attest_gate.py either reword or drop the staleness reason instead of forwarding it, preventing operators from understanding remediation steps.

The composite hash is one-way, so naming changed components requires the old per-component values from the signed manifest (the only trustworthy source of what the reviewer saw), not reconstructed values at read time.
